messages:
From: Oliver Dane <oliver.dane@oxfordbank.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@brightcloud.io
Date: 2028-12-05T08:13:00Z
Subject: Spiking 503/504s + retries — urgent

Hi team,

We're seeing a sustained surge of 503/504s and elevated 429s from the Redwood endpoint serving our UK region starting ~07:50 UTC. Latency has climbed from ~120ms p50 to >2.5s p95, and our client SDKs report retry storms that are compounding the load. This is impacting payment authorizations for a subset of customers and we've already hit our internal SLO for decline rate.

Attached are a few tail logs and a short pcap from one of our edge nodes. Can you confirm whether there was any config push or routing change in the last 24 hours? We need an immediate mitigation or rollback plan — this is P1 for us.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Dane
SRE, Oxford Bank

From: support@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Dane <oliver.dane@oxfordbank.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-05T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Spiking 503/504s + retries — urgent

Hi Oliver — thanks for the report and the logs. We're ingesting the attachments. Initial checks show elevated 503 replies from our EU edge layer and a spike in connection resets to one proxy pool. No automatic config rollout is scheduled, but there was a manual routing diff applied to the EU edge at 07:41 UTC for weighted routing to a new proxy cluster (internal change id: cfg-20281205-17).

We're escalating immediately to the on-call SRE and your AE. I'll attach the raw trace we collected from the ingress for cross-correlation: oxf-logs-20281205.jsonl (attached).

— Redwood Support

Date: 2028-12-05T08:35:00Z
Subject: Escalation: Oxford Bank — regional proxy fanout causing 503/504 wave

Team — Oxford Bank (high-value bank customer) is experiencing a P1 in the EU region. External reported symptoms: elevated 503/504 and 429, retry amplification, and client timeouts impacting payment authorization flows.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: can you validate whether the 07:41 weighted routing to the new proxy cluster produced a cascade (fanout) across the EU pool? If so, can you flip the weight back to previous pool and put the new cluster in drain?
- Grace/CS: please open a dedicated line to Oxford SRE (Oliver) and confirm how many requests/sec are critical to keep auth throughput acceptable; prep the customer-facing update.
- Jonas/Product Ops: we may need to stand up reserved capacity in EU Dedicated for 2 hours while we stabilize — I need a thumbs up for capacity and rough cost estimate.

I'll coordinate exec sync if this requires credits/SLA remediation. Marcus, please paste the quick mitigation steps and ETA in your reply.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Dane <oliver.dane@oxfordbank.com>, support@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-12-05T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: Oxford Bank — regional proxy fanout causing 503/504 wave

Quick tech summary and actions (already executing):
- Root cause hypothesis: the manual routing diff at 07:41 inserted the new proxy cluster into the weighted ring without warming KV caches / backend connections, causing a cold-proxy fanout. The new cluster responded with intermittent 502/503s under load; some clients retried aggressively and amplified the load.
- Immediate mitigations applied (09:00 UTC):
  1) Reverted weighted routing to pre-07:41 weights (cfg rollback initiated).
  2) Drain mode enabled on the new proxy cluster; connections allowed to finish, no new sessions.
  3) Applied temporary ingress rate-limit for Oxford's route (burst 250rps) to limit retry amplification.
  4) Scoped bypass: routed critical payment endpoints to a stable pool in eu-west-1 (direct routing) while health checks finish.
- Monitoring: p50 latency improving; 503 rate down from 3.8% to 0.9% in past 10m. Will keep the rate-limit for 60 minutes and then re-evaluate.
- Next steps (T+30m): warm proxy cluster with synthetic traffic, validate KV cache priming, and reintroduce weighted routing gradually with circuit-breakers.

Attachments: ingress-trace-oxf.pcap (trace snippet showing connection resets)

Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Dane <oliver.dane@oxfordbank.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T09:18:00Z
Subject: Exec note: Oxford Bank P1 — capacity & credit ask

Short exec summary for leadership:
- Impact: Elevated 503/504 wave in EU region affecting authorization throughput for Oxford Bank; customer-facing errors increased for ~35 minutes.
- Root cause: Manual weighted routing introduced an unprimed proxy cluster causing cold fanout.
- Fixes in place: rollback, drain, temporary rate-limit, critical endpoints routed to stable pool. Observed reduction in error rate and latency.
- Ask: approve temporary standby Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 for 2 hours (estimated cost impact: $1,200) to remove any capacity bottlenecks while we fully validate and warm the new cluster. Also authorize standard SLA remediation steps (postmortem + potential service credit discussion) if Oxford requests it.

If approved I will trigger capacity and coordinate the customer post-incident call. ETA for stability: 45–90 minutes.

Jonas Weber
Head, Platform Reliability (interim)

From: Oliver Dane <oliver.dane@oxfordbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Thanks for the rapid response and the clear actions. We've seen a material drop in 503s and timeouts — payment authorizations returned to normal for 99% of traffic after your routing change and the temporary rate limit.

Oxford will take the post-incident call tomorrow; please include a timeline of the config change, the root cause analysis, and the plan to prevent fanout on future cluster joins (warming strategy + circuit breakers). We will also open an internal request for SLA credit; our Head of Ops will follow up separately.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

Oliver Dane
SRE, Oxford Bank
